requirements.statement: A default /implement-trd run (not --chained) runs the code audit (/audit-build, with its fix run) after the end-of-run code review and BEFORE the functional-verification loop, so verification runs once, on code that already carries the audit's fixes. MUST PASS.

could_not_verify: A standalone /audit-build after a satisfied /verify-build closes on code no verification saw, when its fix run changes code (D20, TR4). It is reached only when no deferred close is on record: features built before this change, a Step 7.3 that errored, or an audit that ended open, capped or STUCK. /ship-build's custody check starts at that fix run's head (anchorCommit), so it does not re-prove the fix run's work either. This is today's behaviour, now confined to that case. Not checkable from the text: it is a residual risk the design accepts, seen only in practice. The owner acts: after such an audit, if its readout says the fix run changed code, run /verify-build before shipping.
